lesson_title: Eleven Slips, Six Doors: Running the Whole Books
hook_text: Eleven pieces of paper. Six doors. Ninety seconds. That's real bookkeeping.
clip_script: Friday evening. Thabo tips the month's papers onto the counter: slips, invoices, a debit note, a sad letter about Naidoo. Eleven pieces of paper. Six doors in the back room. The whole job is: every paper through its right door — and the doors ask their own questions. Did money come in? Did money go out? Goods out on trust? Goods in on trust? Anything coming back? And the last paper — no money, no goods — slides through the odd-jobs door, with its explaining sentence. Eleven papers, maybe ninety seconds. Not memorising eleven procedures — just asking two questions eleven times.
visual_style: Top-down counter shot: papers sliding one by one through six glowing doorways, a timer counting down from 90 seconds, the odd letter drifting to a small seventh slot.
pacing: Paper-per-beat rhythm accelerating to the timer's finish.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and run the whole month to a level trial balance.
